## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

High-performance CLI proxy that reduces LLM token consumption by 60-90%

Website • Install • Troubleshooting • Architecture • Discord

English • Francais • 中文 • 日本語 • 한국어 • Espanol

--- rtk filters and compresses command outputs before they reach your LLM context. Single Rust binary, 100+ supported commands, <10ms overhead. ## Token Savings (30-min Claude Code Session) | Operation | Frequency | Standard | rtk | Savings | |-----------|-----------|----------|-----|---------| | `ls` / `tree` | 10x | 2,000 | 400 | -80% | | `cat` / `read` | 20x | 40,000 | 12,000 | -70% | | `grep` / `rg` | 8x | 16,000 | 3,200 | -80% | | `git status` | 10x | 3,000 | 600 | -80% | | `git diff` | 5x | 10,000 | 2,500 | -75% | | `git log` | 5x | 2,500 | 500 | -80% | | `git add/commit/push` | 8x | 1,600 | 120 | -92% | | `cargo test` / `npm test` | 5x | 25,000 | 2,500 | -90% | | `ruff check` | 3x | 3,000 | 600 | -80% | | `pytest` | 4x | 8,000 | 800 | -90% | | `go test` | 3x | 6,000 | 600 | -90% | | `docker ps` | 3x | 900 | 180 | -80% | | **Total** | | **~118,000** | **~23,900** | **-80%** | > Estimates based on medium-sized TypeScript/Rust projects. Actual savings vary by project size. ## Installation ### Homebrew (recommended) ```bash brew install rtk ``` ### Quick Install (Linux/macOS) ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | sh ``` > Installs to `~/.local/bin`. Add to PATH if needed: > ```bash > echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc # or ~/.zshrc > ``` ### Cargo ```bash cargo install --git https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk ``` ### Pre-built Binaries Download from [releases](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/releases): - macOS: `rtk-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` / `rtk-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` - Linux: `rtk-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` / `rtk-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` - Windows: `rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` > **Windows users**: Extract the zip and place `rtk.exe` somewhere in your PATH (e.g. `C:\Users\\.local\bin`). Run RTK from **Command Prompt**, **PowerShell**, or **Windows Terminal** — do not double-click the `.exe` (it will flash and close). For the best experience, use [WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) where the full hook system works natively. 1	# TypeScript Architecture Guidelines
2	
3	Source of truth for code additions/refactors in `resource/ts/`. Read this before writing new code.
4	
5	> Setup-time harness checklist (CLAUDE.md sizing, hooks, allowedTools, skills config) lives in `.claude/SETUP_CHECKLIST.md`. This file is for code-writing decisions.
6	
7	## 1. God objects — current state
8	
9	A god object = single class mixing 3+ reasons to change or > ~600 lines of heterogeneous logic.
10	
11	**Known remaining god objects (planned for separate branch decomposition):**
12	
13	| File | Lines | Reason to split | Status |
14	|---|---|---|---|
15	| `manager/AppManager.ts` | 1950 | Intro + showcase + UI lifecycle + contact flow + debug | Pending (plan: `lovely-humming-spindle.md` Phase 3-1) |
16	| `ui/ContactWizard.ts` | 1445 | Step nav + chip anim + form sync + submission | Dispose leak fixed; split pending (Phase 3-2 partial) |
17	| `pages/works/runtime/WorksPageRuntime.ts` | 1254 | Route lifecycle + scroll + intro + camera + wheel hints | Pending review |
18	| `builder/TimelineBuilder.ts` | 1007 | Declarative GSAP timeline DSL | Size justified (DSL engine) — keep |
19	| `pages/main/theatre/MainTheatreRuntime.ts` | 919 | Theatre sequences + sheet effects + autoplay | Phase 3-4 |
20	| `pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts` | 825 | Layout + render + pointer + view mode | Phase 3-3 |
21	| `pages/about/theatre/AboutTheatreBridge.ts` | 818 | Theatre ↔ scene bindings | Review if splittable by sequence |
22	| `manager/BackgroundManager.ts` | 730 | Env + uniforms + transitions | Acceptable (single rendering concern) |
23	
24	**Healthy coordinators (do not touch):**
25	- `core/Scene.ts`, `core/PageTheatreBinder.ts`, `runtime/PageRuntime.ts` — clean single-purpose orchestrators.
26	- All `types/*.types.ts` — 19 files organized by domain.
27	- All `config/*.config.ts` — constants only, no logic.
28	
29	**Claude rule:** Do not grow the god objects above. New features belong in new runtime/coordinator classes next to them.
30	
31	## 2. How to extend — adding a new feature
32	
33	### Decision tree
34	
35	```
36	New feature needed
37	│
38	├─ Is it a visible 3D object?           → resource/ts/objects/<env|sub|main|rocket|shared>/
39	│                                         Extends SceneObject<TweenProps>
40	│
41	├─ Is it DOM UI (header, modal, form)?  → resource/ts/ui/ or resource/ts/components/
42	│                                         Must implement init() + dispose()
43	│
44	├─ Is it page-scoped runtime state?     → resource/ts/pages/<page>/runtime/
45	│
46	├─ Is it Theatre.js binding for a page? → resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/
47	│                                         Register in PageTheatreBinder factory map
48	│
49	├─ Is it a cross-page orchestrator?     → resource/ts/runtime/ or resource/ts/manager/
50	│                                         Needs strong justification
51	│
52	├─ Is it a shader / material?           → resource/shaders/ + referenced from objects/
53	│
54	└─ Is it a constant / color / URL?      → resource/ts/config/<domain>.config.ts
55	                                          NOT inline
56	```
57	
58	### New scene object checklist
59	
60	1. File: `objects/<group>/YourObject.ts` extending `SceneObject<YourTweenProps>`.
61	2. Implement `runObject()`, `runUpdate(dt)`, `dispose()`, `applyVisibility()`.
62	3. Type: `YourObjectOptions` + `YourTweenProps` in `types/object.types.ts` (not inline).
63	4. Config: constants in `config/<group>.config.ts`.
64	5. Dispose: every allocated geometry/material/texture goes through `utils/disposeObject3D.ts` or `SceneObject._ownedTextures`.
65	6. Registration: `ObjectSetup.ts` for instance + optional `registerObject(id, ...)` for cross-object lookup.
66	
67	### New DOM component checklist
68	
69	1. File: `ui/YourComponent.ts` (singletons) or `components/YourComponent.ts` (reusable widgets).
70	2. Static `init({ root })` + static `dispose()` pair. If multiple instances, keep a `Set<Instance>` and iterate in `dispose()`.
71	3. All event listeners: store bound handlers as fields, remove the same references in `dispose()`.
72	4. Timers: track via `Set<number>` + helper `_trackedTimeout`. Clear all in `dispose()`.
73	5. Web Animations API: track via `Set<Animation>` + helper `_trackAnimation`. Cancel all in `dispose()`.
74	6. Hook into `PageRuntime.dispose()` so page navigation tears down cleanly.
75	7. Options/data types → `types/component.types.ts`.
76	8. CSS class names / selectors → `config/component.config.ts` or `config/dom.config.ts`.
77	
78	### New page route checklist
79	
80	Use `/new-route` skill. Adds:
81	- `routes/web.php` closure route
82	- `views/pages/<page>.php` view
83	- Optional `resource/ts/pages/<page>/` entry
84	
85	## 3. Roles
86	
87	| Folder | Role | What lives here | What does NOT |
88	|---|---|---|---|
89	| `core/` | Engine + scene + lifecycle primitives | `Engine`, `Scene`, `AnimationLoop`, `PostProcessor`, `ModelLoader`, `PageTheatreBinder`, `SceneObject` base | Page-specific logic |

133	### DIP — Dependency Inversion
134	- `Engine` accepts `EngineDependencies` (`sceneFactory`, `modelLoaderFactory`). Use this for testing/swapping.
135	- High-level modules must not `new ConcreteClass()` mid-constructor when a factory slot exists.
136	- Cross-class lookup goes through `context.getObject(id)` (O(1)), never `scene.getObjectByName(...)` (O(n)).

139	Every class that allocates is responsible for releasing:
140	
141	| Creates | Must release in `dispose()` |
142	|---|---|
143	| `addEventListener` | `removeEventListener` with same reference + options |
144	| `setTimeout` / `setInterval` | `clearTimeout` / `clearInterval` |

146	| `new MutationObserver` / Intersection / Resize | `.disconnect()` |
147	| `THREE.BufferGeometry` | `.dispose()` |
148	| `THREE.Material` | `.dispose()` + all texture slots |

168	
169	1. **No `new Vector2/Vector3/Matrix4/Quaternion/Euler` inside `runUpdate`, `render`, or any per-frame callback.**

180	- Before reading `object.matrixWorld` or `object.getWorldPosition()`, call `object.updateWorldMatrix(true, false)` if the render hasn't run yet this frame.

194	- `needsUpdate = true` is set exactly once (after `onBeforeCompile` assignment). Never in the render loop.

201	
202	### Profiling
203

205	- `chrome://tracing` / WebGL Inspector for draw-call counts.
206	- Self-check: 60fps with GC events < 2/sec. Allocation profiler should show ~0 new Vector2/Vector3/Object per frame.

209	
210	The project centralizes all responsive state through `ResponsiveRuntime` (pub/sub). Build new responsive features on top of it; do not add ad-hoc `window.matchMedia` listeners.
211	
212	### Contract
213	
214	```ts
215	const runtime = ResponsiveRuntime.getDefault();
216	const snapshot = runtime.getSnapshot();
217	// snapshot.breakpoint: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
218	// snapshot.viewportWidth / viewportHeight
219	// snapshot.render.clampedPixelRatio
220	// snapshot.device.isMobile
221	// snapshot.reducedMotion
222	// snapshot.performance tier
223	
224	const unsubscribe = runtime.subscribe((next) => {
225	  // react to breakpoint / viewport / reduced motion changes
226	});
227	// In dispose(): unsubscribe();
228	```

231	
232	- **New responsive value:** derive from `snapshot` inside the consumer. Don't add fields to `ResponsiveSnapshot` unless multiple consumers need it.
233	- **Config with breakpoint variance:** use `utils/ResponsiveValue.ts` (`{ sm, md, lg, xl, default }`) — declare in `config/`, resolve at call site.
234	- **Reduced motion:** check `snapshot.reducedMotion` and provide a degraded path (no infinite loops, no parallax). Required for accessibility.
235	- **Pixel ratio / performance tier:** read `snapshot.render.clampedPixelRatio` and `snapshot.performance` — used by `Engine` and `PostProcessor` automatically. Pass the snapshot through, don't re-derive.
236	- **Orientation / mobile only:** prefer `snapshot.device.isMobile` over UA sniffing.

240	
241	- `ResponsiveRuntime._applyCssVariables(snapshot)` publishes CSS custom properties. Read them in SCSS via `var(--vw, 1vw)` etc., not through JS-computed inline styles.
242	
243	### Touch vs hover
244	
245	- Hover UX (`mouseenter` / `mouseleave`) stays on `MouseEvent` semantics — it's desktop-only by design.
246	- Drag / press / click target → `PointerEvent` (`pointerdown` / `pointerup` / `pointermove`) with `pointerId` tracking. See `CustomCursor` and `WorksPageRuntime` patterns.

251	- `matchMedia` listener per component. Use `ResponsiveRuntime.subscribe`.

## 1. God objects — current state

A god object = single class mixing 3+ reasons to change or > ~600 lines of heterogeneous logic.

**Known remaining god objects (planned for separate branch decomposition):**

| File | Lines | Reason to split | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manager/AppManager.ts` | 1950 | Intro + showcase + UI lifecycle + contact flow + debug | Pending (plan: `lovely-humming-spindle.md` Phase 3-1) |
| `ui/ContactWizard.ts` | 1445 | Step nav + chip anim + form sync + submission | Dispose leak fixed; split pending (Phase 3-2 partial) |
| `pages/works/runtime/WorksPageRuntime.ts` | 1254 | Route lifecycle + scroll + intro + camera + wheel hints | Pending review |
| `builder/TimelineBuilder.ts` | 1007 | Declarative GSAP timeline DSL | Size justified (DSL engine) — keep |
| `pages/main/theatre/MainTheatreRuntime.ts` | 919 | Theatre sequences + sheet effects + autoplay | Phase 3-4 |
| `pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts` | 825 | Layout + render + pointer + view mode | Phase 3-3 |
| `pages/about/theatre/AboutTheatreBridge.ts` | 818 | Theatre ↔ scene bindings | Review if splittable by sequence |
| `manager/BackgroundManager.ts` | 730 | Env + uniforms + transitions | Acceptable (single rendering concern) |

**Healthy coordinators (do not touch):**
- `core/Scene.ts`, `core/PageTheatreBinder.ts`, `runtime/PageRuntime.ts` — clean single-purpose orchestrators.
- All `types/*.types.ts` — 19 files organized by domain.
- All `config/*.config.ts` — constants only, no logic.

**Claude rule:** Do not grow the god objects above. New features belong in new runtime/coordinator classes next to them.

## 2. How to extend — adding a new feature

### Decision tree

```
New feature needed
│
├─ Is it a visible 3D object?           → resource/ts/objects/<env|sub|main|rocket|shared>/
│                                         Extends SceneObject<TweenProps>
│
├─ Is it DOM UI (header, modal, form)?  → resource/ts/ui/ or resource/ts/components/
│                                         Must implement init() + dispose()
│
├─ Is it page-scoped runtime state?     → resource/ts/pages/<page>/runtime/
│
├─ Is it Theatre.js binding for a page? → resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/
│                                         Register in PageTheatreBinder factory map
│
├─ Is it a cross-page orchestrator?     → resource/ts/runtime/ or resource/ts/manager/
│                                         Needs strong justification
│
├─ Is it a shader / material?           → resource/shaders/ + referenced from objects/
│
└─ Is it a constant / color / URL?      → resource/ts/config/<domain>.config.ts
                                          NOT inline
```

### New scene object checklist

1. File: `objects/<group>/YourObject.ts` extending `SceneObject<YourTweenProps>`.
2. Implement `runObject()`, `runUpdate(dt)`, `dispose()`, `applyVisibility()`.
3. Type: `YourObjectOptions` + `YourTweenProps` in `types/object.types.ts` (not inline).
4. Config: constants in `config/<group>.config.ts`.
5. Dispose: every allocated geometry/material/texture goes through `utils/disposeObject3D.ts` or `SceneObject._ownedTextures`.
6. Registration: `ObjectSetup.ts` for instance + optional `registerObject(id, ...)` for cross-object lookup.

### New DOM component checklist

1. File: `ui/YourComponent.ts` (singletons) or `components/YourComponent.ts` (reusable widgets).
2. Static `init({ root })` + static `dispose()` pair. If multiple instances, keep a `Set<Instance>` and iterate in `dispose()`.
3. All event listeners: store bound handlers as fields, remove the same references in `dispose()`.
4. Timers: track via `Set<number>` + helper `_trackedTimeout`. Clear all in `dispose()`.
5. Web Animations API: track via `Set<Animation>` + helper `_trackAnimation`. Cancel all in `dispose()`.
6. Hook into `PageRuntime.dispose()` so page navigation tears down cleanly.
7. Options/data types → `types/component.types.ts`.
8. CSS class names / selectors → `config/component.config.ts` or `config/dom.config.ts`.

### New page route checklist

Use `/new-route` skill. Adds:
- `routes/web.php` closure route
- `views/pages/<page>.php` view
- Optional `resource/ts/pages/<page>/` entry

## 3. Roles

| Folder | Role | What lives here | What does NOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| `core/` | Engine + scene + lifecycle primitives | `Engine`, `Scene`, `AnimationLoop`, `PostProcessor`, `ModelLoader`, `PageTheatreBinder`, `SceneObject` base | Page-specific logic |
| `runtime/` | Cross-cutting app-level state machines | `PageRuntime`, `ResponsiveRuntime`, `IntroFlowRuntime`, `ScrollSceneRuntime`, `TimelineRuntime` | Per-page scenes |
| `manager/` | Heavyweight orchestrators | `AppManager` (to be split), `BackgroundManager`, `QaManager`, `IntroManager`, `ShaderManager` | New single-responsibility code (prefer `runtime/` or `core/`) |
| `pages/<page>/runtime/` | Per-page lifecycle | Page-specific scroll, intro, interaction runtimes | Code shared across pages |
| `pages/<page>/scene/` | Per-page THREE.js scene graph wiring | Object composition specific to the page | Generic scene objects |
| `pages/<page>/theatre/` | Per-page Theatre.js bindings | `*TheatreBridge`, `*TheatreRuntime`, `*SceneState` | DOM-only logic |
| `pages/<page>/render/` | Per-page standalone renderers (rare) | `WorksSceneManager` style secondary renderers | Main engine scenes |
| `objects/` | THREE.js scene objects | Classes extending `SceneObject` | DOM elements |
| `ui/` | DOM singletons | `Header`, `Drawer`, `ContactWizard`, `WorkModal`, `IntroCanvas` | Reusable widgets (go to `components/`) |
| `components/` | Reusable DOM widgets | `Button`, `Marquee`, `CustomCursor`, `TextReveal`, `WhySkillPreview` | Scene objects |
| `animation/` | Non-GSAP DOM animation primitives | `TextReveal`, `BlockReveal` base | 3D tweens |
| `builder/` | Declarative composition engines | `TimelineBuilder` | Runtime state |
| `validation/` | Form/input validation | `ContactFormValidation` | Business logic |
| `utils/` | Pure leaf helpers | `disposeObject3D`, `Debounce`, `FrameScheduler`, `Aria`, `Helpers` | Stateful managers |
| `config/` | Constants only | colors, selectors, durations, URLs | Any logic |
| `types/` | Type definitions only | `*.types.ts` per domain | Runtime code |
| `app/` | Bootstrap entry | `AppBootstrap`, `ObjectSetup`, `EnvSetup` | Feature code |
| `lib/` | Third-party wrappers | Theatre.js, Lenis wrappers | Domain code |

Every file must fit one row. If it fits none, stop and reconsider the design.

| Creates | Must release in `dispose()` |

| `requestAnimationFrame` | `cancelAnimationFrame` |
| `new MutationObserver` / Intersection / Resize | `.disconnect()` |
| `THREE.BufferGeometry` | `.dispose()` |
| `THREE.Material` | `.dispose()` + all texture slots |
| `THREE.Texture` | `.dispose()` — or register via `SceneObject._ownedTextures` |
| `THREE.Light` | `.parent?.remove(light)` + `light.dispose?.()` + target removal |
| `Element.animate()` | `.cancel()` |
| Debounce / scheduler | `.offCancel()` |

Use the helpers:
- `utils/disposeObject3D.ts` — traverses an Object3D, disposes geometries + materials (with all 21 texture slots + shader uniform textures).
- `utils/disposeObject3D.ts#removeAndDispose(node)` — detach from parent and dispose.

### Side effects
- Constructors: wiring only. No DOM queries, no RAF, no fetches, no listener registration. Do it in `init()`/`mount()`.
- Module top-level: no side effects. No `window.addEventListener` at import time. No singletons created at import time.
- Static fields: no mutable state. If you need tracking (e.g., `ContactWizard._instances`), it must be reset by a static `dispose()`.

## 5. THREE.js GPU/CPU optimization playbook

### Render-loop hot path rules (hard bans)

1. **No `new Vector2/Vector3/Matrix4/Quaternion/Euler` inside `runUpdate`, `render`, or any per-frame callback.**
   - Use module-scope or instance `_scratch` fields. Mutate with `.copy()`, `.set()`, `.applyMatrix4()`.

```ts
const runtime = ResponsiveRuntime.getDefault();
const snapshot = runtime.getSnapshot();
// snapshot.breakpoint: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"
// snapshot.viewportWidth / viewportHeight
// snapshot.render.clampedPixelRatio
// snapshot.device.isMobile
// snapshot.reducedMotion
// snapshot.performance tier

### CSS integration

### Anti-patterns (do not ship)

- Inline `@media` in TypeScript conditions (`if (window.innerWidth < 768)`). Use the snapshot.
- `matchMedia` listener per component. Use `ResponsiveRuntime.subscribe`.
- Hardcoded breakpoint numbers in TS. Source them from `config/` or from `snapshot.breakpoint`.
- Fighting against `prefers-reduced-motion` (autoplay, infinite animations). Respect it.

content.content: **Scope note:** this only applies to Bash tool calls. Claude Code built-in tools such as `Read`, `Grep`, and `Glob` bypass the hook, so use shell commands or explicit `rtk` commands when you want RTK filtering there. ### Setup ```bash rtk init -g # Install hook + RTK.md (recommended) rtk init -g --opencode # OpenCode plugin (instead of Claude Code) rtk init -g --auto-patch # Non-interactive (CI/CD) rtk init -g --hook-only # Hook only, no RTK.md rtk init --show # Verify installation ``` After install, **restart Claude Code**. ## Windows RTK works on Windows with some limitations. The auto-rewrite hook (`rtk-rewrite.sh`) requires a Unix shell, so on native Windows RTK falls back to **CLAUDE.md injection mode** — your AI assistant receives RTK instructions but commands are not rewritten automatically. ### Recommended: WSL (full support) For the best experience, use [WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) (Windows Subsystem for Linux). Inside WSL, RTK works exactly like Linux — full hook support, auto-rewrite, everything: ```bash # Inside WSL curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | sh rtk init -g ``` ### Native Windows (limited support) On native Windows (cmd.exe / PowerShell), RTK filters work but the hook does not auto-rewrite commands: ```powershell # 1. Download and extract rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip from releases # 2. Add rtk.exe to your PATH # 3. Initialize (falls back to CLAUDE.md injection) rtk init -g # 4. Use rtk explicitly rtk cargo test rtk git status ``` **Important**: Do not double-click `rtk.exe` — it is a CLI tool that prints usage and exits immediately. Always run it from a terminal (Command Prompt, PowerShell, or Windows Terminal). | Feature | WSL | Native Windows | |---------|-----|----------------| | Filters (cargo, git, etc.) | Full | Full | | Auto-rewrite hook | Yes | No (CLAUDE.md fallback) | | `rtk init -g` | Hook mode | CLAUDE.md mode | | `rtk gain` / analytics | Full | Full | ## Supported AI Tools RTK supports 12 AI coding tools. Each integration transparently rewrites shell commands to `rtk` equivalents for 60-90% token savings. | Tool | Install | Method | |------|---------|--------| | **Claude Code** | `rtk init -g` | PreToolUse hook (bash) | | **GitHub Copilot (VS Code)** | `rtk init -g --copilot` | PreToolUse hook — transparent rewrite | | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | `rtk init -g --copilot` | PreToolUse deny-with-suggestion (CLI limitation) | | **Cursor** | `rtk init -g --agent cursor` | preToolUse hook (hooks.json) | | **Gemini CLI** | `rtk init -g --gemini` | BeforeTool hook | | **Codex** | `rtk init -g --codex` | AGENTS.md + RTK.md instructions | | **Windsurf** | `rtk init --agent windsurf` | .windsurfrules (project-scoped) | | **Cline / Roo Code** | `rtk init --agent cline` | .clinerules (project-scoped) | | **OpenCode** | `rtk init -g --opencode` | Plugin TS (tool.execute.before) | | **OpenClaw** | `openclaw plugins install ./openclaw` | Plugin TS (before_tool_call) | | **Mistral Vibe** | Planned ([#800](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/issues/800)) | Blocked on upstream | | **Kilo Code** | `rtk init --agent kilocode` | .kilocode/rules/rtk-rules.md (project-scoped) | | **Google Antigravity** | `rtk init --agent antigravity` | .agents/rules/antigravity-rtk-rules.md (project-scoped) | For per-agent setup details, override controls, and graceful degradation, see the [Supported Agents guide](https://www.rtk-ai.app/guide/getting-started/supported-agents). ## Configuration `~/.config/rtk/config.toml` (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/rtk/config.toml`): ```toml [hooks] exclude_commands = ["curl", "playwright"] # skip rewrite for these [tee] enabled = true # save raw output on failure (default: true) mode = "failures" # "failures", "always", or "never" ``` When a command fails, RTK saves the full unfiltered output so the LLM can read it without re-executing: ``` FAILED: 2/15 tests [full output: ~/.local/share/rtk/tee/1707753600_cargo_test.log] ``` For the full config reference (all sections, env vars, per-project filters), see the [Configuration guide](https://www.rtk-ai.app/guide/getting-started/configuration). ### Uninstall ```bash rtk init -g --uninstall # Remove hook, RTK.md, settings.json entry cargo uninstall rtk # Remove binary brew uninstall rtk # If installed via Homebrew ``` ## Documentation - **[rtk-ai.app/guide](https://www.rtk-ai.app/guide)** — full user guide (installation, supported agents, what gets optimized, analytics, configuration, troubleshooting) - **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)** — detailed installation reference - **[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)** — system design and technical decisions - **[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)** — contribution guide - **[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)** — security policy ## Privacy & Telemetry RTK can collect **anonymous, aggregate usage metrics** once per day. Telemetry is **disabled by default** and requires **explicit opt-in consent** (GDPR Art. 6, 7) during `rtk init` or via `rtk telemetry enable`. This data helps us build a better product: identifying which commands need filters, which filters need improvement, and how much value RTK delivers. For the full list of fields, data handling, and contributor guidelines, see **[docs/TELEMETRY.md](docs/TELEMETRY.md)**. **What is collected and why:** | Category | Data | Why | |----------|------|-----| | Identity | Salted device hash (SHA-256, not reversible) | Count unique installations without tracking individuals | | Environment | RTK version, OS, architecture, install method | Know which platforms to support and test | | Usage volume | Command count (24h), total commands, tokens saved (24h/30d/total) | Measure adoption and value delivered | | Quality | Top 5 passthrough commands (0% savings), parse failure count, commands with <30% savings | Identify missing filters and weak ones to improve | | Ecosystem | Command category distribution (e.g. git 45%, cargo 20%, js 15%) | Prioritize filter development for popular ecosystems | | Retention | Days since first use, active days in last 30 | Understand engagement and detect churn | | Adoption | AI agent hook type (claude/gemini/codex), custom TOML filter count | Track integration coverage and DSL adoption | | Configuration | Whether config.toml exists, number of excluded commands, project count | Understand user maturity and customization patterns | | Features | Usage counts for meta-commands (gain, discover, proxy, verify) | Know which RTK features are valued vs unused | | Economics | Estimated USD savings (based on API token pricing) | Quantify the value RTK provides to users | All data is **aggregate counts or anonymized command names** (first 3 words, no arguments). Top commands report only tool names (e.g. "git", "cargo"), never full command lines. **What is NOT collected:** source code, file paths, command arguments, secrets, environment variables, personal data, or repository contents. **Manage telemetry:** ```bash rtk telemetry status # Check current consent state rtk telemetry enable # Give consent (interactive prompt) rtk telemetry disable # Withdraw consent — stops all collection immediately rtk telemetry forget # Withdraw consent + delete all local data + request server-side erasure ``` **Override via environment:** ```bash export RTK_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 # Blocks telemetry regardless of consent ``` ## Star History ## StarMapper ## Core team - **Patrick Szymkowiak** — Founder [GitHub](https://github.com/pszymkowiak) · [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/patrick-szymkowiak/) - **Florian Bruniaux** — Core contributor [GitHub](https://github.com/FlorianBruniaux) · [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/florian-bruniaux-43408b83/) - **Adrien Eppling** — Core contributor [GitHub](https://github.com/aeppling) · [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adrien-eppling/) ## Contributing Contributions welcome! 이제 충분히 파악했습니다. 결정 포인트가 3개 있어 먼저 확인하고 가는 게 좋겠습니다.

**확인 사실**:
- RTK와 CHOP은 완전히 같은 일(셸 출력 압축)을 함 — 둘 다 `command`를 `tool command`로 바꿔서 LLM 토큰 70~90% 절약
- 누군가가 이미 `.rtk/filters.toml`을 만들고 "migrated from .chop-filters.yml"이라고 적어둠 → 이전 의도가 명확
- Windows 네이티브에서 RTK는 **CLAUDE.md injection 모드**(자동 재작성 X, AI에 룰만 주입). 지금 chop이 동작하는 방식과 정확히 동일
- WSL Ubuntu-24.04 가동 중 — 거기엔 fully-hooked 모드 가능
- 영향 받는 파일: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/settings.json`(PostToolUse hook의 chop 명령어), `.claude/settings.local.json`, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`(글로벌 chop 섹션), `.claude/rules/scss.md` 등 10개

questions.question: CHOP과 RTK 관계를 어떻게 정리할까요? (둘 다 같은 일을 해서 공존시 충돌 가능)

options.label: RTK로 완전 교체 (Recommended)
options.description: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/settings.json/rules의 모든 chop 참조를 rtk로 교체. chop 바이너리는 남겨두되 룰에서 제거. .rtk/filters.toml 주석이 'migrated from'이라고 한 의도 일치

options.label: RTK만 신규로 추가, chop 룰 유지
options.description: chop은 그대로 두고 rtk init만 추가. 두 도구 룰이 공존 → AI가 어느 쪽 prefix 쓸지 매번 헷갈림. 비추천

options.label: 점진적 이전 (RTK는 신규 명령에만, chop은 기존 흐름 유지)
options.description: AGENTS.md에 'rtk를 우선 사용, 기존 chop은 점진 교체'라고 적고 강제 룰은 약화. 마이그레이션 기간만 임시

options.label: Windows 네이티브만 (Recommended)
options.description: rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip을 ~/.local/bin에 설치. 현재 Claude Code(Windows native) 워크플로우와 일치. CLAUDE.md injection 모드(자동 재작성 X) — chop이 동작하는 방식과 동일

options.label: Windows 네이티브 + WSL 둘 다
options.description: 양쪽 모두 설치. WSL에서 작업할 때만 자동 재작성(full hook) 혜택. 향후 WSL 기반 워크플로우로 옮길 옵션 확보. 설치/유지 부담 +1

options.label: WSL만 (Claude Code도 WSL에서 실행)
options.description: WSL Ubuntu-24.04에서 rtk init -g 실행하면 full auto-rewrite hook. 단, 현재 Windows 네이티브로 도는 Claude Code/Cursor를 WSL terminal에서 띄우도록 워크플로우 자체를 바꿔야 함 — 가장 큰 변경

questions.question: 타 프로젝트 재사용 가이드 파일은 어디에 둘까요?

options.label: 글로벌 ~/.claude/templates/rtk-setup.md (Recommended)
options.description: 한 번 만들어 두면 모든 프로젝트에서 참조 가능. 'Docker + Windows 환경에서 RTK 적용' 가이드로 일반화. .claude/BEST_PRACTICES.md/SETUP_CHECKLIST.md 패턴 인용

options.label: 이 repo의 .claude/RTK_GUIDE.md
options.description: 프로젝트 안에 두기. 다른 프로젝트로 옮길 때 복붙해야 함. 버전 관리는 명확

options.label: 양쪽 다 (글로벌은 일반 가이드, 프로젝트는 이 repo 적용 기록)
options.description: 글로벌은 재사용 템플릿, 프로젝트는 'RTK 적용 이력 + 이 repo만의 결정 사항'. 글로벌 가이드가 truth, 프로젝트는 변경분만 기록

# CHOP — Token-Optimized Commands

## Golden Rule

**Always prefix commands with `chop`**. If CHOP has a dedicated filter it uses it; otherwise it passes through unchanged — always safe to use.

```bash
# ✅ Correct (even in chains)
chop git add . && chop git commit -m "msg" && chop git push
```

## Commands by Category

```bash
# Git
chop git status / log / diff / show / add / commit / push / pull / branch / fetch / stash

# Build & Type Check
chop tsc                 # TypeScript errors only
chop npm run <script>    # Compact npm output
chop npx <cmd>

# Files & Search
chop ls <path>
chop grep <pattern>

# Docker
chop docker ps / images / logs <container>

# Meta
chop gain                # Token savings stats
chop gain --history
chop gain --summary
```

## When to Use

Wrap any command that produces noisy output. Skip for commands that output only a few lines.

# RTK 100% 전환 + 다중 프로젝트 BEST PRACTICE 가이드

## Context

- 현재 프로젝트는 **CHOP**(셸 출력 압축 도구, v1.38.1 Windows native)를 광범위하게 강제하는 룰을 운영 중. AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / `.claude/settings.json` PostToolUse 훅 / `.claude/rules` / `.cursor/rules` / `.codex/rules` 10개 파일 + 글로벌 `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` + 메모리 `feedback_chop.md`까지 분산되어 있음.
- 동일 목적의 **RTK**(Rust Token Killer, https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk)가 더 광범위한 100+ 명령 필터·자동 재작성 훅·12종 AI 툴 통합을 제공. 누군가 이미 `.rtk/filters.toml`을 "migrated from .chop-filters.yml" 주석과 함께 만들어 둠 → 이전 의도가 명확.
- 사용자 결정 (이번 세션):
  1. CHOP **100% 제거**, RTK **100% 단일 도구**로 교체
  2. RTK **풀 기능** 환경 = WSL Ubuntu-24.04 (Windows 네이티브는 CLAUDE.md injection만 가능 → 자동 재작성 X)
  3. 타 프로젝트 재사용 가이드는 **BEST PRACTICE 관점** 글로벌 위치 (`~/.claude/templates/rtk-setup.md`)
- 사용자는 Claude Code · Codex · Cursor 3종을 사용. 현재 도커 워크플로우 중심(다른 프로젝트도 도커).
- 환경 사전 점검 완료:
  - WSL Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS 가동, `curl`/`sh`/`git`/`node` 사용 가능
  - WSL 내 Docker 28.0.4 인식(Docker Desktop WSL2 통합 ON)
  - 프로젝트 접근: `/mnt/c/Users/edn_y/renew_nineonelabs`
  - `.rtk/filters.toml` 이미 존재 (4개 필터: docker-compose-logs / docker-compose-php-lint / php-lint / docker-compose-ps)
- **목표 산출물**: ① RTK가 WSL에서 fully-hooked로 동작 ② Claude/Codex/Cursor 3종 모두 RTK init 완료 ③ repo·글로벌·메모리에서 chop 흔적 0 ④ 다른 도커 프로젝트에 그대로 적용 가능한 BEST PRACTICE 문서.

## 결정 사항 요약

| 항목 | 선택 |
|---|---|
| chop 처리 | 완전 삭제(uninstall + 모든 룰 교체) |
| RTK 설치 위치 | WSL Ubuntu-24.04 (`~/.local/bin/rtk`) |
| AI 툴 init | Claude Code(`-g`) + Codex(`-g --codex`) + Cursor(`-g --agent cursor`) |
| 워크플로우 | VS Code · Cursor를 **WSL Remote**로 프로젝트 오픈 (Claude Code 확장이 WSL Linux 환경에서 실행되어 RTK 자동 재작성 훅 적용) |
| 포터블 가이드 | 글로벌 `~/.claude/templates/rtk-setup.md` (BEST_PRACTICES 톤) |
| 프로젝트 훅 | `.claude/settings.json` PostToolUse `chop tsc` → `rtk tsc` |

## 작업 순서

### Phase A — WSL에 RTK 설치 + 3종 AI 툴 초기화

1. WSL 셸 진입(`wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04`) 후 다음을 순차 실행:
   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | sh
   echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
   source ~/.bashrc
   rtk --version          # 0.28.x 확인
   rtk gain               # 분석 명령 동작 확인
   ```
2. AI 툴 초기화 (WSL 내, 어떤 디렉토리에서 실행해도 글로벌 설정):
   ```bash
   rtk init -g                        # Claude Code: PreToolUse 훅 + RTK.md 글로벌
   rtk init -g --codex                # Codex: AGENTS.md + RTK.md 인스트럭션
   rtk init -g --agent cursor         # Cursor: hooks.json
   rtk init --show                    # 설치 검증
   ```
3. WSL 측 글로벌 Claude 설정(`~/.claude/settings.json`)에 RTK 훅이 들어갔는지 확인. 충돌이 있으면 사용자가 수동 머지(이번에는 WSL `~/.claude`가 fresh일 가능성이 높음 → init이 깔끔히 작성).
4. `rtk` 텔레메트리는 default disabled. opt-in 묻는 프롬프트가 뜨면 사용자 판단(권장: disable, 사적 명령 흐름 노출 우려).

### Phase B — VS Code · Cursor를 WSL Remote로 전환

이 단계가 빠지면 RTK 훅이 Windows 네이티브 Claude Code에 닿지 않아 "100% 사용 환경" 요건 미달.

1. VS Code: 좌하단 ⟨⟩ 원격 인디케이터 → "Connect to WSL" → 디스트로 `Ubuntu-24.04` 선택 → 폴더 열기 `/mnt/c/Users/edn_y/renew_nineonelabs`.
2. Claude Code 확장이 자동으로 WSL-Server 모드로 재기동. 이때부터 Bash 도구 호출은 WSL bash를 거쳐 RTK 훅이 적용됨.
3. Cursor: 동일하게 "Open Folder in WSL". Cursor도 `~/.cursor/hooks.json`을 WSL 측에 사용.
4. Codex CLI: WSL 터미널에서 `codex` 실행. 프로젝트 루트에 진입한 상태에서 `rtk init --show`로 활성 확인.
5. 검증 절차(아래 Phase E)를 WSL Remote 세션에서 실행.

> **주의**: WSL 기본 사용자가 root인지 비root인지 사전에 확인. `whoami` 결과가 `root`라면 `~/.local/bin/rtk`는 `/root/.local/bin/rtk`. Claude/Cursor가 WSL Remote에서 실행되면 같은 사용자로 동작하므로 정합. 비root 추가 사용자가 따로 있다면 그쪽에도 설치 반복 필요.

### Phase C — CHOP 흔적 0으로 만들기 (repo + 글로벌 + 메모리 + 바이너리)

#### C-1. Repo 파일 (10개) 일괄 교체

## 작업 순서

### Phase A — WSL에 RTK 설치 + 3종 AI 툴 초기화

1. WSL 셸 진입(`wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04`) 후 다음을 순차 실행:
   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | sh
   echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
   source ~/.bashrc
   rtk --version          # 0.28.x 확인
   rtk gain               # 분석 명령 동작 확인
   ```
2. AI 툴 초기화 (WSL 내, 어떤 디렉토리에서 실행해도 글로벌 설정):
   ```bash
   rtk init -g                        # Claude Code: PreToolUse 훅 + RTK.md 글로벌
   rtk init -g --codex                # Codex: AGENTS.md + RTK.md 인스트럭션
   rtk init -g --agent cursor         # Cursor: hooks.json
   rtk init --show                    # 설치 검증
   ```
3. WSL 측 글로벌 Claude 설정(`~/.claude/settings.json`)에 RTK 훅이 들어갔는지 확인. 충돌이 있으면 사용자가 수동 머지(이번에는 WSL `~/.claude`가 fresh일 가능성이 높음 → init이 깔끔히 작성).
4. `rtk` 텔레메트리는 default disabled. opt-in 묻는 프롬프트가 뜨면 사용자 판단(권장: disable, 사적 명령 흐름 노출 우려).

### Phase B — VS Code · Cursor를 WSL Remote로 전환

이 단계가 빠지면 RTK 훅이 Windows 네이티브 Claude Code에 닿지 않아 "100% 사용 환경" 요건 미달.

1. VS Code: 좌하단 ⟨⟩ 원격 인디케이터 → "Connect to WSL" → 디스트로 `Ubuntu-24.04` 선택 → 폴더 열기 `/mnt/c/Users/edn_y/renew_nineonelabs`.
2. Claude Code 확장이 자동으로 WSL-Server 모드로 재기동. 이때부터 Bash 도구 호출은 WSL bash를 거쳐 RTK 훅이 적용됨.
3. Cursor: 동일하게 "Open Folder in WSL". Cursor도 `~/.cursor/hooks.json`을 WSL 측에 사용.
4. Codex CLI: WSL 터미널에서 `codex` 실행. 프로젝트 루트에 진입한 상태에서 `rtk init --show`로 활성 확인.
5. 검증 절차(아래 Phase E)를 WSL Remote 세션에서 실행.

> **주의**: WSL 기본 사용자가 root인지 비root인지 사전에 확인. `whoami` 결과가 `root`라면 `~/.local/bin/rtk`는 `/root/.local/bin/rtk`. Claude/Cursor가 WSL Remote에서 실행되면 같은 사용자로 동작하므로 정합. 비root 추가 사용자가 따로 있다면 그쪽에도 설치 반복 필요.

   ```bash

   echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc
   rtk --version
   ```
4. **Per-AI init (실행할 것만 골라 실행)**
   ```bash
   rtk init -g                       # Claude Code
   rtk init -g --codex               # Codex
   rtk init -g --agent cursor        # Cursor

   - 한 줄짜리 추가 패턴 예시.
7. **Hook integration (PostToolUse)** — TypeScript 프로젝트 예시:
   ```json
   {
     "matcher": "Edit|Write",
     "hooks": [{
       "type": "command",
       "command": "node -e \"...; execSync('rtk tsc --noEmit', ...)\""
     }]
   }
   ```

## 위험 / 롤백

- **WSL Remote 전환 자체가 워크플로우 변경**: 재기동 후 첫 세션은 일부 VS Code 확장이 WSL 측에 다시 깔리느라 잠깐 느림 (1회성).

# Claude Code Harness Setup Checklist

One-time setup health check for the Claude Code harness in this project. Code-writing guidelines live in `.claude/BEST_PRACTICES.md`.

---

## 1. CLAUDE.md

- [x] Under 50 lines? — Yes (post-2026-04-25 slim)
- [x] Does not contain anything Claude can infer from reading the code (file structure, naming conventions, etc.)?
- [x] File-type rules are separated into `.claude/rules/`?
- [x] Explicit "do not" prohibition patterns listed?
- [x] Verification commands included (tsc, lint, test, etc.)?

## 2. Rules (`.claude/rules/`)

- [x] Split by file extension? (`php.md`, `frontend.md`, `scss.md`)
- [x] Each rules file has a `paths:` frontmatter header?
- [x] Rules contain only things that cannot be inferred from the code?

## 3. Hooks (`.claude/settings.json`)

- [x] Auto-runs tsc after editing a `.ts` file?
- [x] Hook verified to actually fire by editing a `.ts` file?
- [x] Frequently used safe commands registered in `allowedTools`?

## 4. Skills (`.claude/skills/`)

- [x] Repeatable workflows packaged as skills?
- [x] Project-specific workflows like `/migration`, `/new-route` defined?

## 5. Subagents (`.claude/agents/`)

- [x] Exploration agents available for read-heavy tasks?
- [x] Three.js scene exploration delegated to `scene-explorer` agent?
- [x] PHP structure exploration delegated to `php-explorer` agent?

## 6. Session habits

- [ ] Using `/clear` between unrelated tasks?
- [ ] After two failed corrections, starting fresh with `/clear` + better prompt?
- [ ] Protecting main context by asking "use a subagent to investigate"?
- [ ] Resuming long sessions with `--continue` / `--resume`?

## 7. Token waste patterns (fix immediately if found)

- [x] No docs/ folder accumulating content Claude can infer from code?
- [x] CLAUDE.md not exceeding 50 lines?
- [ ] Claude prefixing Bash tool calls with `chop`? (verify with `chop gain`)
- [ ] `chop gain` count increasing? Zero means chop is not actually being used.

---

## Current project setup status

| Item | Status |
| --- | --- |
| CLAUDE.md concise | ✅ |
| CLAUDE.md skill invocation examples | ✅ |
| Rules on-demand | ✅ php / frontend / scss |
| Hooks (tsc) | ✅ Node.js stdin pattern |
| Hook verified | ✅ Confirmed firing via Edit tool on .ts file |
| allowedTools | ✅ chop / git / tsc / docker / npm test |
| Skills | ✅ migration / new-route |
| Subagents | ✅ scene-explorer / php-explorer |
| docs/ removed + README cleaned | ✅ |
| spatie/image WEBP optimization | ✅ 1.10.6 (PHP 7.4 compat), ImageProcessor, dockerfile libwebp-dev |
| CHOP applied | ✅ |
| MEMORY.md | ✅ architecture / workflow / chop / npm / permissions |
| Test framework | ✅ vitest (19 tests) |
| --dangerously-skip-permissions | ✅ VS Code setting (allowDangerouslySkipPermissions) |
| npm build/watch/install forbidden | ✅ AGENTS.md / frontend.md (CLAUDE.md inherits via @AGENTS.md) |
| All AI-read files in English | ✅ |

## Permission setup — `allowDangerouslySkipPermissions`

To prevent Claude Code from asking for permission on every action, enable via VS Code:

1. Open **File → Preferences → Settings** (or `Ctrl+,`)
2. Search for `claudeCode.allowDangerouslySkipPermissions`
3. Check the box — this adds "Bypass permissions" to the mode cycle

> **Warning:** This flag auto-approves all tool use: file writes, Bash execution, etc.
> Use only in trusted projects. Default permission mode is recommended for unfamiliar codebases.

## Why npm build commands are forbidden

`npm run build`, `npm run watch`, and `npm install` are **forbidden during normal development**.

- **Reason:** Vite dev server at `http://localhost:8888` auto-rebuilds the bundle on every file save
- Running these wastes context and time with no benefit
- **Exception:** `npm install <package>` — only when explicitly adding a new dependency
- This rule lives in two places: `AGENTS.md` (cross-AI canonical) and `.claude/rules/frontend.md` (Claude auto-load on `.ts`/`.tsx` edits). CLAUDE.md inherits via `@AGENTS.md` import.

## How the tsc PostToolUse hook works

When a `.ts` file is modified via the Edit or Write tool, the PostToolUse hook fires automatically:

```bash
# Command executed by the hook
chop node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
```

- Hook config: `.claude/settings.json` → `PostToolUse` → matcher: `Edit|Write`
- If tsc errors are found, the hook returns `exit(1)`, immediately notifying Claude
- **How to verify:** Edit any `.ts` file with the Edit tool → check hook output for tsc results

---
name: new-route
description: Add a new public page route, view, and optional TypeScript entry
disable-model-invocation: true
argument-hint: <description>
---

Add a new public page for: $ARGUMENTS

1. Register route in `routes/web.php`:

```php
$router->get('/path', function () {
    return render('pages.section.index', $data);
})->name('name');
```

2. Create view at `views/pages/<section>/index.php`
   - Do NOT include layout chrome — that comes from `views/layouts/main.php`
   - Set `data-page` attribute if the page needs a TypeScript strategy

3. If Three.js / managed page needed:
   - Add scene config: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/<page>.scene.ts`
   - Register strategy in `resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts`
   - Add theatre folder: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`

4. Run type check after any `.ts` changes:

```bash
chop node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit   # errors only
```

# NINEONELABS Codex Guide

Cross-AI repo rules. Claude reads this via `CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md` import. File-type details additionally live in `.claude/rules/{frontend,php,scss}.md` (Claude auto-loads by `paths:` frontmatter; Codex should read them on-demand for the matching extension).

## Brand Identity

See `BRAND.md` first for the brand routing index. Do not load the full `brand/*.md` set by default — read only files needed for the task.

- Company: **NINEONELABS (나인원랩스)** — digital web agency
- Core values: **Experiment · Challenge · Proof** (실험 · 도전 · 증명)
- Concept: Earth → Planet NX-2 voyage. NINEONELABS is the companion (조력자), not the captain.
- Slogan: **JOIN THE JOURNEY** — use as-is for display contexts
- Services: APP · WEB · BRANDING · UI/UX · MAINTENANCE
- Space metaphor is the frame, not the message — always land on the concrete agency offer
- Display name: `NINEONELABS` (uppercase). Technical: `nineonelabs` only for files/slugs/code. Korean: `나인원랩스`. Never mixed camel case.
- Never position NINEONELABS as an aerospace/aviation entity

## Project Defaults

- Stack: TypeScript, SCSS, Three.js, Vite, PHP 7.4 custom MVC, MySQL, Apache via Docker
- Dev server: `http://localhost:8888`
- Default task framing: state goal, context, constraints, done condition. Plan first for complex/ambiguous work.
- **Forbidden commands**: `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, `npm install` — Vite auto-rebuilds on save. Only `npm install <package>` is allowed when adding a new dependency. Never list these in roles, plans, verification steps, or PR notes.
- Prefer `chop` for output that may exceed a few lines (git, search, typecheck, docker, PowerShell pipelines). Examples: `chop git status`, `chop git diff`, `chop git log --oneline -20`, `chop rg ...`, `chop powershell -Command "..."`. Short one-liners may skip `chop`.
- Windows PowerShell: explicit UTF-8 for Korean text reads/writes.

## Architecture

- Public routes are closure-based in `routes/web.php` and render via `render()`. Do not reintroduce Barba.js or SPA navigation contracts.
- Ownership separation: do not duplicate work in `AppManager`, `PageRuntime`, or `PageTheatreBinder`. See `.claude/BEST_PRACTICES.md` Part A and memory `project_ts_map.md` for boundaries.
- Page scenes: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`. Theatre bindings: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`. Page-scoped runtime: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/runtime/`. Shared types: `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`. Keep shared engine/runtime code out of page folders.
- Image uploads: entry point `imageUpload()` in `inc/lib/func.php`. Auto-creates `.webp` sibling via `\Core\ImageProcessor::makeWebpSibling()`. DB stores the original filename. New upload paths that bypass `imageUpload()` must call `makeWebpSibling()` after `move_uploaded_file()`. Detail in `.claude/rules/php.md`.
- `Core\ImageProcessor` (`src/Core/ImageProcessor.php`): WEBP via spatie/image 1.10.6 (GD). jpg/jpeg/png/gif covered; svg/ico skipped. Resize threshold 2560px. Quality 82.

## Editing Rules

- Follow existing custom MVC patterns; no Laravel/Symfony conventions.
- SCSS: BEM naming. Use shared `fluid(min, max)` over raw responsive values. `var(--token, fallback)` is forbidden — use `var(--token)` or `fluid(...)` directly. Full SCSS rules in `.claude/rules/scss.md`.
- TypeScript/Three.js: dispose every geometry/material/texture; no object creation in render loops; match `addEventListener` with `removeEventListener`. Full rules in `.claude/rules/frontend.md`.
- PHP: closure routing, `nb_` table prefix, migrations only for schema changes. Full rules in `.claude/rules/php.md`.
- Never hardcode credentials or secrets.

## Verification

- TypeScript: `chop node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`
- PHP lint: `docker compose exec web php -l <file>`
- Diff: `chop git diff`
- After changes: smallest relevant verification + report any skipped checks.
- Never use npm build/watch/install for verification — saved files are already handled by Vite.

## Repo Skills

- `$scene-explorer` — Three.js scene/Theatre/runtime ownership
- `$php-explorer` — routes, render chains, admin, schema
- `/migration <desc>` (Claude slash command) — DB schema change
- `/new-route <desc>` (Claude slash command) — new public page

## Codex Notes

- Repo config: `.codex/config.toml`
- Repo execution policy: `.codex/rules/default.rules`
- Codex hooks intentionally omitted (disabled on Windows)
- Direct terminal commands not auto-wrapped — use `chop <command>` explicitly
- Keep this file concise and durable. Add rules only after repeated friction.
- Stable repo rules belong here; use skills for repeatable workflows; MCP only for external fast-changing context.

# RTK — Token-Optimized Commands

## Golden Rule

**Use `rtk` for any command whose output may exceed a few lines.** Inside WSL Remote sessions the global PreToolUse hook auto-rewrites Bash commands to their `rtk`-prefixed form (`git status` → `rtk git status`). On native Windows shells the hook is unavailable, so prefix explicitly. `rtk` passes through commands without a dedicated filter unchanged — always safe to use.

```bash
# ✅ Correct (chains too)
rtk git add . && rtk git commit -m "msg" && rtk git push
```

## Commands by Category

```bash
# Git
rtk git status / log / diff / show / add / commit / push / pull / branch / fetch / stash

# GitHub CLI
rtk gh pr list / view / create
rtk gh issue list / view
rtk gh run list

# Build & Type Check
rtk tsc                  # TypeScript errors only, grouped by file
rtk lint                 # ESLint grouped by rule/file
rtk next build           # Next.js build compact

# Tests
rtk test <cmd>           # generic — failures only
rtk vitest / jest / pytest / cargo test / go test

# Files & Search
rtk ls <path>            # token-optimized tree
rtk read <file>          # smart file read
rtk grep <pattern> <path>
rtk find "*.ext" <path>
rtk diff <a> <b>

# Containers
rtk docker ps / images / logs / compose ps / compose logs
rtk kubectl pods / logs / services

# Data & Errors
rtk json <file>          # structure without values
rtk err <cmd>            # filter errors only from any command
rtk log <file>           # deduplicated log
rtk env -f <prefix>      # filtered env vars
rtk curl <url>           # truncate + save full output

# Meta
rtk gain                 # token savings stats
rtk gain --history       # recent commands
rtk gain --daily         # day-by-day breakdown
rtk discover             # find missed savings opportunities
rtk init --show          # verify which AI tool integrations are active
```

## When to Use

Wrap any noisy command (`git`, `docker`, `tsc`, test runners, `find`, log files). Skip for commands that produce only a handful of lines. RTK passes through unknown commands transparently.

## Setup Reference

For installing RTK in a fresh project (Docker + WSL workflow), see `~/.claude/templates/rtk-setup.md`.

name: RTK token optimization — mandatory prefix
description: All Bash commands prefer `rtk` prefix; WSL Remote sessions auto-rewrite via PreToolUse hook, native Windows requires explicit prefix
type: feedback
---

Prefix Bash commands with `rtk` whenever output may exceed a few lines.

**Why:** Noisy output (`git`, `tsc`, `docker`, test runners, file dumps) wastes the context window. RTK filters/compresses to 10–40% of the original size — 60–90% token savings on a typical 30-min session. Replaced CHOP entirely (2026-04-25) — chop is uninstalled, all rules now reference rtk.

**How to apply:**
- WSL Remote (recommended): the global Claude Code PreToolUse hook (registered by `rtk init -g` inside WSL) auto-prefixes — no manual action needed.
- Native Windows shells (Git Bash, PowerShell): the hook does not run, so prefix explicitly. `rtk git status`, `rtk tsc --noEmit`, `rtk docker compose ps`, `rtk grep ...`.
- Short outputs (<5 lines, e.g. `git rev-parse HEAD`) may skip `rtk`.
- Project-level filters: `.rtk/filters.toml` overrides global behavior for `docker compose logs`, `php -l`, etc.
- Verify usage: `rtk gain` (zero counter ⇒ rtk not actually being invoked).

# RTK Setup — Portable BEST PRACTICE

Reusable setup guide for installing RTK ([rtk-ai/rtk](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk)) in any Docker-based project, optimized for the Windows + WSL2 + Docker Desktop workflow that matches my dev environment. Drop into any new project: read top-to-bottom, run the commands, you're done in ~5 minutes.

> RTK = "Rust Token Killer". Single Rust binary, filters/compresses 100+ shell command outputs before they reach the LLM. Typical 30-min Claude Code session: ~118k tokens → ~24k. MIT licensed, <10ms overhead.

## 1. Why RTK in every project

- 60–90% token savings on noisy commands (`git`, `tsc`, `docker`, test runners, log files).
- One global install covers all projects; per-project `.rtk/filters.toml` adds project-specific patterns.
- Replaces ad-hoc shell wrappers (CHOP and similar) — single source of truth, supported across 12 AI coding tools.
- Auto-rewrite is **transparent**: in WSL Remote sessions the AI never sees the rewrite, just gets compact output. No prompt engineering or rule memorization required.

## 2. Prerequisites

| Platform | Mode | Setup notes |
|---|---|---|
| **macOS / Linux** | Full auto-rewrite | Install via Homebrew or curl, run `rtk init -g`, done. |
| **Windows + WSL2** (this guide's primary target) | Full auto-rewrite **only inside WSL Remote sessions** | Install RTK in WSL, open VS Code/Cursor with WSL Remote → AI uses WSL bash → hook fires. |
| Native Windows (Git Bash / PowerShell) | Explicit `rtk` prefix only — no auto hook | Use only when WSL Remote isn't an option. |

For Docker projects on Windows: Docker Desktop's WSL2 backend already runs your containers in WSL, so adopting WSL Remote for the editor is a natural extension — no new infrastructure.

## 3. One-shot install (run inside WSL)

```bash
# Inside WSL (any distro with curl + sh + git)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | sh
grep -q '$HOME/.local/bin' ~/.bashrc || \
  echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
rtk --version    # Expect 0.37.x or newer
```

`install.sh` writes the binary to `~/.local/bin/rtk`. No sudo needed.

## 4. Per-AI init (run only the lines for tools you actually use)

Each command writes/edits the corresponding global config file inside WSL (`/root/.claude/`, `/root/.cursor/`, `/root/.codex/`). They're idempotent and leave existing config untouched.

```bash
# Pre-create config dirs once (rtk fails if these don't exist)
mkdir -p ~/.claude ~/.cursor ~/.codex ~/.config/rtk

# Claude Code — PreToolUse hook + RTK.md + @RTK.md import in CLAUDE.md
rtk init -g --auto-patch

# Cursor — preToolUse hook in ~/.cursor/hooks.json
rtk init -g --agent cursor --auto-patch

# Codex — AGENTS.md + RTK.md instructions (no hook; instruction-based)
rtk init -g --codex      # interactive, no --auto-patch flag here

# Optional: other AI tools
rtk init -g --gemini --auto-patch
rtk init -g --copilot --auto-patch

# Verify what's wired up (Claude/Cursor/OpenCode shown; Codex is file-based, check ~/.codex/)
rtk init --show
```

After each init, **restart the AI tool** to pick up the new config.

## 5. VS Code / Cursor → WSL Remote

This step is what unlocks full auto-rewrite for Windows users.

1. Install the **WSL** extension in VS Code (or the equivalent in Cursor).
2. Bottom-left status bar → click `><` → **Connect to WSL** → select your distro.
3. Open the project folder via WSL path: `/mnt/c/...` for projects on Windows drive, or `~/projects/...` for projects you've moved into WSL ext4 (faster IO).
4. The AI extension (Claude Code / Cursor) re-installs into the WSL server and now invokes Bash via WSL → RTK hook fires.

**Test it works**: open a chat, type `git status`. Tool log should show the call as `rtk git status`.

## 6. Project-level filters template

Drop this at `<project>/.rtk/filters.toml` for any Docker + PHP/Node project. Filters layer on top of RTK's built-ins — no overlap with `rtk git`, `rtk tsc`, `rtk docker ps` (those have native handlers).

```toml
schema_version = 1
# Project-level RTK filters

[filters.docker-compose-logs]
description = "Filter docker compose logs to relevant lines"
match_command = "^docker compose logs\\b"
strip_ansi = true
strip_lines_matching = ["^(?!web\\s+\\||db\\s+\\|).*(?<!(error|warn|warning|exception|fatal|critical|traceback|deprecated|notice|apache|php))$"]
max_lines = 120

[filters.docker-compose-php-lint]
description = "PHP lint via docker compose — errors/warnings only"
match_command = "^docker compose exec web php -l\\b"
strip_ansi = true
strip_lines_matching = ["^(?!.*(no syntax errors detected|parse error|fatal error|warning|notice)).*$"]

[filters.php-lint]
description = "PHP lint — errors/warnings only"
match_command = "^php -l\\b"
strip_ansi = true
strip_lines_matching = ["^(?!.*(no syntax errors detected|parse error|fatal error|warning|notice)).*$"]

[filters.docker-compose-ps]
description = "docker compose ps — first 20 lines"
match_command = "^docker compose ps\\b"
strip_ansi = true
max_lines = 20
```

Adapt service names (`web`, `db`) to your compose file. Add a `vite-dev` filter if you tail Vite logs frequently.

## 7. Hook integration: PostToolUse type-check

For TypeScript projects, run `tsc --noEmit` after every edit so the AI gets compile feedback on every save. Drop into `.claude/settings.json` (Claude Code project-level):

```json
{
  "allowedTools": ["Bash(rtk *)", "Bash(git *)"],
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "node -e \"let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{try{const i=JSON.parse(d);const f=(i.tool_input&&i.tool_input.file_path)||'';if(f.endsWith('.ts')||f.endsWith('.tsx')){const {execSync}=require('child_process');try{execSync('rtk tsc --noEmit',{stdio:'inherit',cwd:process.cwd()})}catch(e){process.exit(1)}}}catch(e){}});\""
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`rtk tsc --noEmit` returns errors only, grouped by file — minimal noise in the hook output. The hook runs inside the WSL session when the project is opened via WSL Remote.

## 8. Repository rule files (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / .cursor/rules)

Add a single bullet to your repo-level rule docs so future AI sessions know to use rtk:

```markdown
- Prefer `rtk` for output that may exceed a few lines (git, search, typecheck, docker, test runners). Examples: `rtk git status`, `rtk git diff`, `rtk tsc --noEmit`, `rtk docker compose ps`. WSL Remote sessions auto-rewrite via the global PreToolUse hook; native Windows shells require explicit prefix.
```

Place this in:
- `AGENTS.md` (cross-AI canonical) — Codex + Claude both read it
- `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` if Cursor users edit the project
- Project-level `CLAUDE.md` only if Claude needs deltas beyond AGENTS.md

## 9. Verification checklist

Run from inside the WSL Remote session:

- [ ] `rtk --version` → 0.37.x or newer
- [ ] `which rtk` → `/root/.local/bin/rtk` (or `~/.local/bin/rtk`)
- [ ] `rtk init --show` → Claude/Cursor/(OpenCode) hooks show `[ok]`
- [ ] In a fresh AI chat, ask the AI to run `git status` → tool log shows `rtk git status`
- [ ] `rtk docker compose ps` (with the filters.toml above) outputs ≤ 20 lines
- [ ] Edit a `.ts` file → PostToolUse hook fires `rtk tsc --noEmit` (visible in Claude Code session log)
- [ ] `rtk gain` after a few minutes of work → savings counter > 0

## 10. Migrating from CHOP

If a project currently mandates CHOP, run this migration once per project:

1. Replace strings: `grep -rl 'chop' .claude .cursor .codex AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` then sed `chop` → `rtk` (review each match — some are documentation prose, not commands).
2. Update `.claude/settings.json`:
   - `allowedTools`: `Bash(chop *)` → `Bash(rtk *)`
   - PostToolUse hook command: `chop ...` → `rtk ...`
3. Convert `.chop-filters.yml` → `.rtk/filters.toml` (RTK uses TOML with `schema_version = 1`).
4. Uninstall CHOP binary:
   - Windows: delete `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Programs\chop\` and remove that path from system PATH (Win+R → `sysdm.cpl` → Advanced → Environment Variables → User PATH).
   - WSL: nothing to do unless you separately installed it inside the distro.
5. Verify zero residual: `grep -ri chop .claude .cursor .codex AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` returns nothing.
6. Remove memory entries: `feedback_chop.md` (if any), update `MEMORY.md` index line.

## 11. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| AI runs `git status` raw, not `rtk git status` | Not in WSL Remote, or hook not registered | `rtk init --show` to verify; reconnect VS Code with WSL Remote |
| `rtk gain` always 0 | rtk binary never invoked (e.g., Windows native session) | Check `which rtk`; ensure bash session sources `~/.bashrc` |
| `rtk init -g` fails: "No such file or directory" | `~/.claude` (or `~/.cursor`/`~/.codex`) not yet created | `mkdir -p ~/.claude ~/.cursor ~/.codex` and re-run |
| Hook fires but output is unfiltered | Custom filter regex mismatched | Test with `rtk proxy <command>` to confirm RTK sees it; check `match_command` regex |
| Telemetry prompt during init | Default disabled, asks for opt-in | Decline (`rtk telemetry disable`) or `export RTK_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` permanently in `~/.bashrc` |

## 12. Uninstall

```bash
rtk init -g --uninstall      # Remove hook + RTK.md + settings.json entry
rtk init -g --codex --uninstall   # if Codex was wired up
rm ~/.local/bin/rtk          # remove binary
rm -rf ~/.config/rtk         # remove global filters
# project-side: remove .rtk/filters.toml and any rtk references in rule docs
```

max_lines = 120

[filters.docker-compose-php-lint]
description = "PHP lint via docker compose — errors/warnings only"
match_command = "^docker compose exec web php -l\\b"
strip_ansi = true
strip_lines_matching = ["^(?!.*(no syntax errors detected|parse error|fatal error|warning|notice)).*$"]

[filters.php-lint]
description = "PHP lint — errors/warnings only"
match_command = "^php -l\\b"
strip_ansi = true
strip_lines_matching = ["^(?!.*(no syntax errors detected|parse error|fatal error|warning|notice)).*$"]

[filters.docker-compose-ps]
description = "docker compose ps — first 20 lines"
match_command = "^docker compose ps\\b"
strip_ansi = true
max_lines = 20
```

Adapt service names (`web`, `db`) to your compose file. Add a `vite-dev` filter if you tail Vite logs frequently.

## 7. Hook integration: PostToolUse type-check

For TypeScript projects, run `tsc --noEmit` after every edit so the AI gets compile feedback on every save. Drop into `.claude/settings.json` (Claude Code project-level):

```json
{
  "allowedTools": ["Bash(rtk *)", "Bash(git *)"],
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "node -e \"let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{try{const i=JSON.parse(d);const f=(i.tool_input&&i.tool_input.file_path)||'';if(f.endsWith('.ts')||f.endsWith('.tsx')){const {execSync}=require('child_process');try{execSync('rtk tsc --noEmit',{stdio:'inherit',cwd:process.cwd()})}catch(e){process.exit(1)}}}catch(e){}});\""
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`rtk tsc --noEmit` returns errors only, grouped by file — minimal noise in the hook output. The hook runs inside the WSL session when the project is opened via WSL Remote.

## 8. Repository rule files (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / .cursor/rules)

Add a single bullet to your repo-level rule docs so future AI sessions know to use rtk:

```markdown
- Prefer `rtk` for output that may exceed a few lines (git, search, typecheck, docker, test runners). Examples: `rtk git status`, `rtk git diff`, `rtk tsc --noEmit`, `rtk docker compose ps`. WSL Remote sessions auto-rewrite via the global PreToolUse hook; native Windows shells require explicit prefix.
```

Place this in:
- `AGENTS.md` (cross-AI canonical) — Codex + Claude both read it
- `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` if Cursor users edit the project
- Project-level `CLAUDE.md` only if Claude needs deltas beyond AGENTS.md

## 9. Verification checklist

Run from inside the WSL Remote session:

- [ ] `rtk --version` → 0.37.x or newer
- [ ] `which rtk` → `/root/.local/bin/rtk` (or `~/.local/bin/rtk`)
- [ ] `rtk init --show` → Claude/Cursor/(OpenCode) hooks show `[ok]`
- [ ] In a fresh AI chat, ask the AI to run `git status` → tool log shows `rtk git status`
- [ ] `rtk docker compose ps` (with the filters.toml above) outputs ≤ 20 lines
- [ ] Edit a `.ts` file → PostToolUse hook fires `rtk tsc --noEmit` (visible in Claude Code session log)
- [ ] `rtk gain` after a few minutes of work → savings counter > 0

## 10. Migrating from CHOP

If a project currently mandates CHOP, run this migration once per project:

1. Replace strings: `grep -rl 'chop' .claude .cursor .codex AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` then sed `chop` → `rtk` (review each match — some are documentation prose, not commands).
2. Update `.claude/settings.json`:
   - `allowedTools`: `Bash(chop *)` → `Bash(rtk *)`
   - PostToolUse hook command: `chop ...` → `rtk ...`
3. Convert `.chop-filters.yml` → `.rtk/filters.toml` (RTK uses TOML with `schema_version = 1`).
4. Uninstall CHOP binary:
   - Windows: delete `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Programs\chop\` and remove that path from system PATH (Win+R → `sysdm.cpl` → Advanced → Environment Variables → User PATH).
   - WSL: nothing to do unless you separately installed it inside the distro.
5. Verify zero residual: `grep -ri chop .claude .cursor .codex AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` returns nothing.
6. Remove memory entries: `feedback_chop.md` (if any), update `MEMORY.md` index line.

## 11. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| AI runs `git status` raw, not `rtk git status` | Not in WSL Remote, or hook not registered | `rtk init --show` to verify; reconnect VS Code with WSL Remote |
| `rtk gain` always 0 | rtk binary never invoked (e.g., Windows native session) | Check `which rtk`; ensure bash session sources `~/.bashrc` |
| `rtk init -g` fails: "No such file or directory" | `~/.claude` (or `~/.cursor`/`~/.codex`) not yet created | `mkdir -p ~/.claude ~/.cursor ~/.codex` and re-run |
| Hook fires but output is unfiltered | Custom filter regex mismatched | Test with `rtk proxy <command>` to confirm RTK sees it; check `match_command` regex |
| Telemetry prompt during init | Default disabled, asks for opt-in | Decline (`rtk telemetry disable`) or `export RTK_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` permanently in `~/.bashrc` |

## 12. Uninstall

```bash
rtk init -g --uninstall      # Remove hook + RTK.md + settings.json entry
rtk init -g --codex --uninstall   # if Codex was wired up
rm ~/.local/bin/rtk          # remove binary
rm -rf ~/.config/rtk         # remove global filters
# project-side: remove .rtk/filters.toml and any rtk references in rule docs
```

1	# NINEONELABS Codex Guide
2	
3	Cross-AI repo rules. Claude reads this via `CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md` import. File-type details additionally live in `.claude/rules/{frontend,php,scss}.md` (Claude auto-loads by `paths:` frontmatter; Codex should read them on-demand for the matching extension).
4	
5	## Brand Identity
6	
7	See `BRAND.md` first for the brand routing index. Do not load the full `brand/*.md` set by default — read only files needed for the task.
8	
9	- Company: **NINEONELABS (나인원랩스)** — digital web agency
10	- Core values: **Experiment · Challenge · Proof** (실험 · 도전 · 증명)
11	- Concept: Earth → Planet NX-2 voyage. NINEONELABS is the companion (조력자), not the captain.
12	- Slogan: **JOIN THE JOURNEY** — use as-is for display contexts
13	- Services: APP · WEB · BRANDING · UI/UX · MAINTENANCE
14	- Space metaphor is the frame, not the message — always land on the concrete agency offer
15	- Display name: `NINEONELABS` (uppercase). Technical: `nineonelabs` only for files/slugs/code. Korean: `나인원랩스`. Never mixed camel case.
16	- Never position NINEONELABS as an aerospace/aviation entity
17	
18	## Project Defaults
19	
20	- Stack: TypeScript, SCSS, Three.js, Vite, PHP 7.4 custom MVC, MySQL, Apache via Docker
21	- Dev server: `http://localhost:8888`
22	- Default task framing: state goal, context, constraints, done condition. Plan first for complex/ambiguous work.
23	- **Forbidden commands**: `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, `npm install` — Vite auto-rebuilds on save. Only `npm install <package>` is allowed when adding a new dependency. Never list these in roles, plans, verification steps, or PR notes.
24	- Prefer `rtk` for output that may exceed a few lines (git, search, typecheck, docker, PowerShell pipelines). Examples: `rtk git status`, `rtk git diff`, `rtk git log --oneline -20`, `rtk grep ...`, `rtk docker compose ps`. Short one-liners may skip `rtk`. In WSL Remote sessions the PreToolUse hook auto-rewrites `git`/`docker`/`tsc`/etc. to their `rtk`-prefixed equivalents.
25	- Windows PowerShell: explicit UTF-8 for Korean text reads/writes.
26	
27	## Architecture
28	
29	- Public routes are closure-based in `routes/web.php` and render via `render()`. Do not reintroduce Barba.js or SPA navigation contracts.
30	- Ownership separation: do not duplicate work in `AppManager`, `PageRuntime`, or `PageTheatreBinder`. See `.claude/BEST_PRACTICES.md` Part A and memory `project_ts_map.md` for boundaries.
31	- Page scenes: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`. Theatre bindings: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`. Page-scoped runtime: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/runtime/`. Shared types: `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`. Keep shared engine/runtime code out of page folders.
32	- Image uploads: entry point `imageUpload()` in `inc/lib/func.php`. Auto-creates `.webp` sibling via `\Core\ImageProcessor::makeWebpSibling()`. DB stores the original filename. New upload paths that bypass `imageUpload()` must call `makeWebpSibling()` after `move_uploaded_file()`. Detail in `.claude/rules/php.md`.
33	- `Core\ImageProcessor` (`src/Core/ImageProcessor.php`): WEBP via spatie/image 1.10.6 (GD). jpg/jpeg/png/gif covered; svg/ico skipped. Resize threshold 2560px. Quality 82.
34	
35	## Editing Rules
36	
37	- Follow existing custom MVC patterns; no Laravel/Symfony conventions.
38	- SCSS: BEM naming. Use shared `fluid(min, max)` over raw responsive values. `var(--token, fallback)` is forbidden — use `var(--token)` or `fluid(...)` directly. Full SCSS rules in `.claude/rules/scss.md`.
39	- TypeScript/Three.js: dispose every geometry/material/texture; no object creation in render loops; match `addEventListener` with `removeEventListener`. Full rules in `.claude/rules/frontend.md`.
40	- PHP: closure routing, `nb_` table prefix, migrations only for schema changes. Full rules in `.claude/rules/php.md`.
41	- Never hardcode credentials or secrets.
42	
43	## Verification
44	
45	- TypeScript: `rtk tsc --noEmit` (or `rtk node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`)
46	- PHP lint: `rtk docker compose exec web php -l <file>` (matches `php-lint` filter in `.rtk/filters.toml`)
47	- Tests: `rtk npm run test` (Vitest single run — `vitest run`, not `watch`)
48	- Diff: `rtk git diff`
49	- After changes: smallest relevant verification + report any skipped checks.
50	- Never use npm build/watch/install for verification — saved files are already handled by Vite.
51	
52	### Test discipline
53	
54	- Bug fix: write a **failing test that reproduces the bug first**, then fix until it passes. No fix without a regression test.
55	- New pure utility / helper / validator (`utils/`, `validation/`, etc.): tests precede or land with the implementation in the same change. Stateful runtime/UI is exempt — Vitest is unit-only here.
56	- Test files: co-located `*.test.ts` next to the source (matches existing Vitest setup). No `__tests__/` folder convention.
57	- Before commit: `rtk npm run test` and `rtk tsc --noEmit` must both be green. Skipping either requires an explicit note in the report.
58	
59	## Repo Skills
60	
61	- `$scene-explorer` — Three.js scene/Theatre/runtime ownership
62	- `$php-explorer` — routes, render chains, admin, schema
63	- `/migration <desc>` (Claude slash command) — DB schema change
64	- `/new-route <desc>` (Claude slash command) — new public page
65	
66	## Codex Notes
67	
68	- Repo config: `.codex/config.toml`
69	- Repo execution policy: `.codex/rules/default.rules`
70	- Codex hooks intentionally omitted (disabled on Windows)
71	- Direct terminal commands not auto-wrapped — use `rtk <command>` explicitly
72	- Keep this file concise and durable. Add rules only after repeated friction.
73	- Stable repo rules belong here; use skills for repeatable workflows; MCP only for external fast-changing context.
